fit: oral ethanolic rhizome extract and mouse maze behavior
assessment: Open-arm occupancy increased at both tested extract doses. The paper reports no significant 60-minute locomotor difference but gives no numerical locomotor values. No fresh grated or clinical Parkinson contrast.

fit: ginger extract and mouse dark-box anxiety model
assessment: Open-arm time means were greater after extract. The same experiment describes movement differences and gives no extract preparation method, route or dosing duration.

fit: oral aqueous extract of supermarket ginger and rat maze
assessment: Open-arm time averaged 30 versus 20 seconds, with no significant open-field crossing difference. Filtered extract and a rat maze cannot identify a clinical effect of eating grated ginger.

fit: clove powder and hot-water nociception in mice
assessment: The annual report gives no analgesic effect in the hot-water assay. It prints 1 mg/kg powder, leaves that assay route unstated and provides no group counts, effect sizes or uncertainty.

fit: topical clove oil cream and chronic anal fissure healing
assessment: The author abstract reports 60% versus 12% healing at three months and lower manometric pressures. The full paper is needed to verify a pain outcome separately.

fit: injected clove essential oil and mouse hot-plate behavior
assessment: Three essential-oil concentrations gave higher transformed latency responses than saline. The route was intraperitoneal and the outcome thermal response in mice.

fit: injected clove oil and mouse nociception
assessment: The oil group showed fewer writhes and longer hot-plate latency than saline. The article mentions sedation with higher doses. No ground clove or clinical Parkinson outcome.

fit: topical clove-derived eugenol and acute toothache
assessment: At five minutes 14/17 eugenol and 0/17 vehicle participants reported relief. Allocation and blinding details and uncertainty are unreported. The exposure was a constituent gel applied at the painful site.

fit: oral aqueous clove extract and experimental nociception
assessment: The author abstract reports favorable assay results overall and leaves species and test-level comparisons unclear. Publisher full article download returned 404.
